text: The error 'connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:11434' means the machine resolves localhost to IPv6 while Ollama listens on IPv4. Change the base URL to http://127.0.0.1:11434. (high confidence)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: Per an independent July 2026 guide, the Ollama Model node suits simple prompt-response in a Basic LLM Chain and cannot connect to the AI Agent node; agent workflows need the Ollama Chat Model node. The guide warns not every Ollama model does reliable function calling: smaller or older models may mangle tool calls, invent parameters or ignore tools. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-20)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: The community stack coleam00/local-ai-packaged bundles n8n and Ollama with Supabase, Open WebUI, Flowise, Qdrant, Neo4j, SearXNG, Caddy and Langfuse via start_services.py profiles (gpu-nvidia, gpu-amd, cpu, none). In it n8n reaches Ollama at http://ollama:11434. On Apple Silicon Docker cannot use the GPU, so run Ollama natively with profile none and point the n8n credential at http://host.docker.internal:11434/. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-26)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: In n8n sub-nodes (such as the Ollama chat model node), expressions like {{ $json.name }} always resolve to the first input item, unlike root nodes which resolve per item. (medium confidence)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: Community reports (May 2026) say AI Agent workflows with local Ollama models often output tool schemas as plain text instead of executing tool calls (about 9 in 10 runs across ~10 models); qwen3.5 4b+ worked best but slowly. No cause was confirmed; suggested mitigations were a larger model, a LiteLLM proxy and checking tool schema format. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-03)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: n8n's Ollama credential supports only the Instance URL method. Fields are Base URL (default http://localhost:11434) and an optional API key sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header, meant for authenticated remote proxies such as Open WebUI. The credential serves the Ollama, Chat Ollama and Embeddings Ollama nodes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: If only n8n runs in Docker, set Ollama to bind 0.0.0.0 on the host and use http://host.docker.internal:11434 as base URL. On Linux without Docker Desktop, start n8n with --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway (or compose extra_hosts host.docker.internal:host-gateway). (high confidence)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: If n8n and Ollama run in separate containers, use the Ollama container name as host (e.g. http://my-ollama:11434) and make sure Ollama binds 0.0.0.0. If only Ollama is in Docker, publish -p 11434:11434 and keep localhost. (high confidence)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: n8n docs state Ollama does not support custom HTTP agents, so HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY may not work for the n8n Ollama nodes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama

text: Ollama's docs describe connecting n8n to Ollama Cloud: create an API key on ollama.com, add an Ollama credential in n8n, set API URL to https://ollama.com and paste the key. The n8n credential page does not mention Ollama Cloud. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: n8n and workflow automation with Ollama
